change: Algorithm 2 dispatch-side sequence ownership, on top of the A+B request lifecycle / accounting identity patch
b_root_cause: _evict_all_waiting_requests released the staged list only after an early return that an empty waiting queue took, so a staged request survived a deactivation and its sequence was never retired. The release and its report now run before any return; the Redis drain the early return exists for is unchanged.
a_identity: The ordinary BackendAdmitReq tagged itself with self.model_name, which follows the reused worker slot rather than the request. It now carries the model Algorithm 2 scheduled the request under, matching what 84f880f already does for adoption grants.

c_i_reuse.decision: keep the frozen c_i; stage 01 is NOT re-run
c_i_reuse.why: The c_i profiling arm launches a solo server with no --enable-gpu-scheduler, --enable-controller or --enable-moore-hodgson, so _alg2_runtime_gate is False and the dispatch ledger is never populated. _handle_mh_migrated_away, _mh_scheduler_retired_rids, scheduler_retired_unacked and backend_admit_after_retire appear zero times in final_profile_ci.sh and profile_v2.py, and a solo profile performs no deactivation. The watchdog patch touches monitor_baseline_stage.py, which the c_i stage does not invoke (0 references). Stage 01 STATUS remains PASS from 2026-08-22T18:29:17Z and its artifacts are untouched.

ownership_invariant: A dispatched Algorithm 2 sequence is owned by the GPU scheduler until the backend acknowledges admission; after that acknowledgement ownership passes to the engine-side lifecycle accounting.

dispatch_seq_ownership.root_cause: A sequence issued at dispatch for a request the engine never fetched was invisible to every retirement path: the engine cannot report a request it never held, and the backend drain found an empty queue. GPU 0's frontier froze on seq 1159 (model_4#140) for the rest of the run while the request itself was re-dispatched on GPU 1 as seq 2110 and served.
dispatch_seq_ownership.fix: On a model departure the GPU scheduler retires the sequences it still owns for that model -- dispatched, not yet acknowledged -- through the existing _mh_retired_admit_seqs / _mh_retired_start_seqs and the existing contiguous-prefix drain. Already-acknowledged requests are untouched and remain the engine-side lifecycle's responsibility.
dispatch_seq_ownership.race_handling: An acknowledgement, prefill start or completion still in flight when the sequence was retired names a tombstoned rid: it is recognised as already accounted exactly once, logged, and moves no frontier. It is not an ordering violation. A tombstone is cleared when the same rid is dispatched again on that GPU, so a returning request is always governed by its live record.
dispatch_seq_ownership.call_site_audit: Every MigratedAwayReq originates from the deactivate handler (scheduler.py:1993 and :2055 call _evict_all_waiting_requests; _drain_backend_queue is reached only from it; the kv-stash report is inside _v6_stash_captured). There is no path that reports a request as gone while its model stays resident, so the sweep can never retire a live sequence of a resident model.
